news.title: Looped transformers reuse attention memory to improve compact-model efficiency
news.summary: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer selectively reuses attention keys and values across repeated layer passes. Authors report 1.7× validation-loss token efficiency for their 700M model against OLMo3 under a 400B-token pretraining experiment.
news.why_it_matters: May improve the quality attainable per training token while reducing redundant loop computation.
news.caveat: Author-reported comparison at selected scales; validation loss is not end-user intelligence, wall-clock speed or independent reproduction.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Monitor safety scores depend strongly on how evaluation cases are generated
news.summary: In a controlled study of a former production monitor, measured missed-detection rates changed substantially across evaluation conditions. The authors warn against interpreting a narrow test suite as a deployment guarantee.
news.why_it_matters: Safety evaluations need diverse, justified threat models and held-out cases.
news.caveat: A controlled evaluation of one monitor, not an observed deployment incident or a general estimate of current monitor performance.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Multi-user voice benchmark tests privacy, attribution and shared task completion
news.summary: Mu-Bench evaluates full-duplex voice assistants using 800 simulated cases across 20 domains. In the authors' 13-system study, tested open-weight systems scored below 20% joint success, and larger groups were harder to coordinate.
news.why_it_matters: Single-user voice accuracy can conceal failures when several speakers have different permissions and goals.
news.caveat: Simulated participants and benchmark-specific criteria; not a real-world privacy incident or a definitive ranking.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Driving-policy post-training targets remaining failure conditions
news.summary: Researchers repeatedly generate targeted scenarios based on a model's remaining failures. In one sealed simulation test, the collision-free fraction for ReCogDrive rose from 0.390 to 0.765; a small real-vehicle demonstration also improved.
news.why_it_matters: Adaptive data generation could help teams focus training on rare difficult cases without a large deployed fleet.
news.caveat: Specific scenarios and very small real-vehicle trial; not proof of roadworthiness or general safety.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Deep-research benchmark measures breadth and depth of evidence coverage
news.summary: DRBench Pro builds structured knowledge rubrics from Wikipedia. In 144 cases across 24 domains, the authors report that the strongest of 16 tested agents covered about 57% on their combined metric.
news.why_it_matters: Separates topical coverage from the depth of related explanations rather than relying only on a holistic judge.
news.caveat: Wikipedia-derived knowledge and rubric design may bias results; coverage does not establish factual correctness or exhaustive research.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Agent memory can fail even when retrieval succeeds
news.summary: Researchers distinguish cases where retrieved facts are ignored, associated with the wrong subject, or confused with obsolete versions. Their TASK Memory approach combines external text with activation steering and editable model knowledge.
news.why_it_matters: Highlights a failure beyond retrieval recall: whether the model uses the right information at generation time.
news.caveat: Preprint with five tested open models; intervention side effects, portability and persistent-memory privacy need separate evaluation.
news.publication_date_basis: v1 submission November 25; publicly listed November 26; exact public posting time not verified

news.title: Together releases Hurdle for repeatable coding-agent integration tests
news.summary: The npm library runs coding agents on developer-defined tasks under varying models and initial conditions. It supports programmatic checks, restrictions on actions and rubric-based judging, with optional isolated runs.
news.why_it_matters: Teams can test whether their APIs, documentation and skills actually help agents complete real workflows.
news.caveat: Publisher describes the library as open source; exact license and security isolation not independently audited. Sandboxed runs and model access can incur charges.

news.title: AWS previews Transcribe Turbo with speech-aware turn detection
news.summary: AWS announces an updated speech recognition model with context hints and end-of-turn detection for English streaming. It reports roughly 14% relative English streaming word-error reduction versus its production model; English batch is already generally available in most regions.
news.why_it_matters: Combining speech and language cues may reduce awkward interruptions in real-time voice interfaces.
news.caveat: Vendor metrics; streaming preview in US East (Ohio), language and region availability vary, and interruption behavior requires application-specific testing.

news.title: AWS previews checkpointed orchestration for isolated code execution
news.summary: A Lambda durable-functions extension can coordinate individual or stateful MicroVM tasks, retry failures and checkpoint progress, including parallel isolated environments.
news.why_it_matters: Agent-generated code can be separated from the workflow controller while retaining multi-step recovery.
news.caveat: Developer preview explicitly not intended for production; isolation is not a complete security guarantee. Requires regions supporting both services.

news.title: DeepMind packages chemistry tools as Antigravity skills
news.summary: Mass Spec Skills connects Gemini reasoning with established mass-spectrometry software and chemical databases to propose candidate molecular structures and explain supporting evidence.
news.why_it_matters: Specialized computational tools can make scientific agents more useful than a standalone language model for exact calculations and retrieval.
news.caveat: Candidate structures need expert and experimental verification; performance depends on spectrum quality and database coverage, and vendor claims are not independently replicated.

news.title: Targeted translation distillation narrows a Lao-language capability gap
news.summary: Together reports that an adapter trained on teacher-generated Lao and Thai translations improved a 27B student's Lao chrF++ from 5.5 to 44.3 on 1,012 sentences, versus 47.5 for the teacher, while preserving Thai performance. The full experiment series reportedly cost $260.
news.why_it_matters: Mixing retention examples with new-language data can reduce regressions during narrow capability transfer.
news.caveat: Company case study; 93% refers to a translation metric ratio, not general model capability. Costs and teacher-output rights must be independently assessed.

news.title: New York signs a temporary prohibition on chatbot toys
news.summary: The state Senate records S9408A as signed on November 24, chapter 416. Subsequent November 25 coverage reports a five-year moratorium on manufacturing, distributing and selling covered chatbot toys, beginning 90 days after signing.
news.why_it_matters: Product safety and privacy requirements increasingly affect AI systems embedded in children's physical products.
news.caveat: Scope and exceptions depend on statutory definitions; signing is not immediate enforcement. Reported product risks are not universal to all toys.
news.publication_date_basis: Legislative action date verified; page first publication unknown; Guardian report dated November 25

news.title: Reuters reports possible Chinese model-development delays under compute restrictions
news.summary: Reuters reports that tighter access to overseas advanced-chip compute and restrictions on model-output distillation could delay upcoming model releases at Z.AI and Moonshot AI, according to people familiar with the companies.
news.why_it_matters: Compute access and training-data policy can alter model release cadence and costs.
news.caveat: Attributed reporting from unnamed sources; future timelines are not confirmed company commitments. Exact rule text and company responses require separate verification.

terms.name: Use-time memory hallucination
terms.definition: An agent produces an answer inconsistent with a relevant memory that was successfully retrieved, or applies that memory to the wrong subject.
terms.mechanism: Generation may favor parametric knowledge, confuse stored versions or misbind a retrieved fact to an entity.
terms.example: An assistant retrieves a corrected meeting location but outputs the old location stored in its earlier context.
terms.caveat: Different from retrieval failure; the source proposes a taxonomy, not a universally established diagnostic.

terms.name: Joint task success
terms.definition: In Mu-Bench, an evaluation criterion that requires every participant's task goal, privacy requirement and terminal condition to hold together.
terms.mechanism: Scores a case as successful only when all specified constraints are met, rather than averaging independently completed goals.
terms.example: A shared voice assistant must complete both users' permitted requests without revealing private details.
terms.caveat: Benchmark-specific operational definition; similar joint-success metrics may exist under other names.
